question: What is the structure of NodeAffinity in the Kubernetes API, and how do required versus preferred scheduling rules differ?

ground_truth.answer: NodeAffinity defines node label-based scheduling constraints for a Pod. requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution is a NodeSelector (hard constraint) — the Pod is not scheduled if no matching node exists. preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution is a list of PreferredSchedulingTerm (soft preference) — the scheduler tries to satisfy them but schedules elsewhere if not met. A NodeSelector contains nodeSelectorTerms (list of NodeSelectorTerm, OR-combined); each NodeSelectorTerm has matchExpressions (list of NodeSelectorRequirement, AND-combined) with key, operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt), and values fields. Each PreferredSchedulingTerm has weight (1–100) and preference (NodeSelectorTerm).
context: io.k8s.api.core.v1.NodeAffinity: requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution (NodeSelector, hard) and preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution (list of PreferredSchedulingTerm, soft)
io.k8s.api.core.v1.NodeSelector: nodeSelectorTerms is a list of NodeSelectorTerm (OR-combined)
io.k8s.api.core.v1.NodeSelectorRequirement: key, operator (In/NotIn/Exists/DoesNotExist/Gt/Lt), and values define a single label constraint within a term
